patch.value: MCP update keys and CLI update flags diverge in name (linkedFile/linkedTest vs --file/--test), so an agent that reads the MCP contract and writes a CLI command produces a guaranteed unknown-option refusal

Every MCP declared key resolves to a CLI flag, via a shared name or a registered alias; A parity gate fails when an MCP declared key has no CLI flag or alias that accepts it; The unknown-option recovery names the accepted flag for a known cross-surface synonym
1. Read the pm_update declared keys, which list linkedFile and linkedTest  2. Run pm update <id> --linked-file path=a.ts  3. Refusal: Unknown option --linked-file
One name per concept across MCP and CLI, or an alias so a contract-derived name always parses.

The MCP contract advertises linkedFile/linkedTest; the CLI accepts only --file/--test. The refusal is well-formed but the agent had no way to know from the contract it just read, and the recovery does not name the correct flag.

Unify MCP update keys and CLI update flags through the shared contract vocabulary so linkedFile and linkedTest resolve to accepted CLI spellings or registered aliases. Add cross-surface parity enforcement and actionable unknown-option recovery without removing either capability.
